To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a human-machine collaborative semi-supervised learning model to identify extremist posts in social media using a small amount of annotated data and a large collection of un-annotated data.

a) our proposed framework is able to achieve high accuracy in the classification of malicious social media posts, and b) it requires significantly fewer labeled data than fully supervised learning methods.

our proposed framework is a novel, human-machine collaborative, interactive learning system, that uses a multi-view context-aware, graph-based subset optimization method to efficiently identify malicious social media content and its principal influencers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a dynamic learning framework that is robust against limited ground truth data and can be easily updated to reflect the evolution of TTPs.
the identification of the key suspects, the key threats and the associated key posts that are associated with criminal activity in online communities.
the design, development and evaluation of a novel, dynamic learning framework that is capable of identifying malicious posts in the social media with expressions of extremism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed method is a novel approach to identifying extremist content in social media that is robust, efficient, effective, and scalable.

the proposed method is a promising solution to the problem of online extremism identification, which is an important step towards the development of an automated system that can effectively identify and mitigate online extremism.

our framework is a promising approach to the identification of extreme online content, which is an important step toward identifying the key influencers and threats associated to criminal activity and extremism on the web.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an effective and dynamic framework to identify extreme online posts with expressions of extremism and criminal intent.
our framework can be used for the development and refinement of classifiers to identify malicious social media post with expressions of extremism and criminal intent.

we propose a human-machine collaborative framework to identify malicious social media post in presence of limited ground truth data, unstructured data, and constantly evolving tactics and procedures of criminal activity and terrorism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method can efficiently and effectively detect malicious posts in social media with limited annotated data.

, by using a subset optimization method and multi-view context-aware learning framework, our proposed system is capable of learning from limited labeled data and evolving into a sophisticated classifier with a reasonably acceptable accuracy.

the framework can robustly identify online posts with expressions of extremism, criminal intent, or malicious activities, with limited annotated data and without the need to manually identify the key suspects and threats.
